text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.04% today to $387, continuing a strong week-long rally that's added 7.3% since late August. The primary driver is geopolitical tension in the Middle East: Iran has launched retaliatory strikes against U.S. Gulf allies including Kuwait, pushing crude oil prices higher (Brent above $95, U.S. crude at $91.48). For a refiner like Marathon, higher oil prices typically improve profit margins when combined with strong refinery utilization—the sector is running at 98% capacity right now—because the company can sell refined products (gasoline, diesel) at prices that don't fall in line with crude cost increases.

The rally also reflects genuine tightness in energy markets heading into this escalation. With over 17 million barrels of oil transiting the Hormuz Strait daily and concerns about potential supply disruption, the inventory picture matters: gasoline and diesel stocks are moderate (205.7 million and 104.2 million barrels respectively), leaving little cushion if Middle East supply shocks worsen. Refiners benefit from the combination of higher prices and the operational leverage of running flat-out to meet demand.
